text: Working together with community partners, the SDO will continue to keep its curriculum aligned with the digital landscape and remain a key touchpoint for Singaporeans needing digital assistance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One good example is the SDO's collaboration with the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, RLAF partners 20 mosques to organise training sessions that equip seniors with applicable digital skills, such as staying connected through Facebook, WhatsApp and Zoom.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The participants I spoke with at one of the sessions greatly appreciated the hands-on learning environment, in a safe space amongst friends.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Foundation intends to expand their outreach to more mosques and deepen learning for seniors who have already picked up basic smartphone skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: RLAF also plans to work with other community partners, like Roses of Peace, to scale their efforts by supplementing volunteers, curating curriculum and launching a certification system to reward the seniors for their learning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Many other partners have stepped forward to support our seniors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MCI will continue to bridge digital knowledge and skills gaps, to help citizens keep pace with digitalisation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The digital landscape is continually changing, with new technologies and new apps.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We aim to imbue in Singaporeans, a sense of confidence to continue to adapt to this changing space, to actively participate in the digital domain and confidently take on new digital opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We plan to achieve this in two ways.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: First, by harnessing the community's reach, energy and resources through the Digital for Life movement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, the Digital for Life Fund was established to provide funding assistance for ground-up digital inclusion initiatives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One example is Byte.SG, which runs the "Void Deck Technology Labs Initiative".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through building skills and familiarity in science and technology topics, Byte.SG aims to bring technology awareness to children living in rental flats.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At one of Byte.SG's recent sessions, I saw how the team used augmented reality (AR) and interactive online tools to bring the underwater world to life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Not only were the children excited by this, I was also fascinated by the demonstration!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Supported by the Digital for Life Fund, Byte.SG will scale their initiative to locations, such as Nanyang, Bedok, Tanjong Pagar and Tampines, to help more children build digital confidence in a fun, empowering manner.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With our 3P partners, we will build on the Digital for Life movement and continue mobilising efforts on the ground by organising a series of events and activities in the coming months.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This will culminate in a Digital for Life Festival, which will take place in the middle of the year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Second, MCI is helping our people deepen digital skills through our libraries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our libraries and archives are important learning marketplaces to pique Singaporeans' curiosity and inspire discovery, at every stage of our lives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the face of digitalisation, our libraries must keep up with the times, to continue bringing citizens a wide array of learning opportunities, as pointed out by Ms Jessica Tan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Many Members have visited NLB's LAB25 showcase in the main lobby and I encourage the rest to drop by if you have not done so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The showcase brings to life LAB25's four focus areas: building a learning marketplace, nurturing an informed citizenry, inspiring Singapore storytellers and being an equaliser in society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A new Singapore Alcove showcasing Singapore stories and literature will be part of the Central Public Library after its revamp.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It will be a "home" for the Singapore collection with regular programming by local authors, featuring immersive and experiential exhibits.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Building on NLB's ongoing efforts to ensure accessibility of its physical spaces, NLB will do more through a comprehensive suite of accessibility services for persons with disabilities, starting at Punggol Regional Library.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes accessible collections comprising sensory and Braille books, sign language with text, and books that are useful for caregivers on social and life skills and assistive technologies, such as "Immersive Readers" to cater to Singaporeans with different language needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the same time, NLB is continually working to improve the physical spaces in our libraries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Central Public Library and Marine Parade Public Library will be revamped later this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To encourage Singaporeans to actively take charge of their learning, NLB will make more resources and content available to wider audiences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Jessica Tan will be pleased to note that NLB will roll out Nodes in everyday spaces, such as offices, food and beverage outlets and parks around Singapore to provide new entry points for citizens to access digital resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As extensions of physical libraries, these Nodes will showcase NLB's digital collections, to interest Singaporeans to read and learn wherever they can.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked about our efforts to encourage young readers to master their mother tongue languages.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB continues to source for, select and identify new avenues to grow their mother tongue language content.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Recently, NLB has begun offering award-winning English children's books translated into the vernacular.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB also proactively encourages local publishers to publish their mother tongue language titles in both print and electronic formats to help widen access.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to deliver the next segment of my speech in Malay, please.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In Malay):   Digitalisation has impacted our lives in many ways and it has brought many opportunities and possibilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As digitalisation becomes more prevalent, it is also important that the Government scale up efforts to empower the community in terms of their digital capabilities and well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Together with the 3P partners, the Government will provide digital access and enhance digital readiness, promote the learning and mastery of digital skills through our libraries, and equip our people, especially the vulnerable, to identify and deal with online risks and threats.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As we step up efforts to empower the community, I am heartened to see that many Singaporeans have taken the bold step to learn new digital skills and contribute to this development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One example is a network comprising more than 300 individuals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They share career opportunities and workshops that are available in the technology sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In fact, some individuals in this network came from non-technology sectors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, one is from the healthcare administration sector and has now become a technology developer of augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This transition took place after they witnessed how the pandemic had affected hands-on learning conducted physically and they began to realise the value of applying digital technology.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I had the opportunity to speak to one of the network members, Mr Mohd Afiq.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He is the founder of Playtours, an online tool that allows users to create unique and meaningful virtual experiences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include "escape room" games and real-time multi-player games.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Developing a product from scratch is certainly not an easy task.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, Afiq is confident of the value that "Playtours" will bring to today's digital world and this has encouraged him to persevere and carry on in order to develop his business.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is clear that individuals like Afiq serve as an inspiration to all of us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Let us be inspired as well, so that we can, together, seize the digitalisation opportunities that await us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, the third key goal that MCI is working towards is to ensure that our people are equipped to recognise and respond to dangers online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The digital way of life often remains challenging, novel and unfamiliar to many of us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Recent events, such as phishing scams, may have also caused us to be wary of going digital.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But we cannot let these fears hold us back from unlocking new opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Rather, we must actively equip ourselves with the relevant knowledge and skills to embrace technological advancements, with the ability to recognise and respond to the risks in the digital domain.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I agree with Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, Dr Shahira Abdullah, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Don Wee that it is ever more important to ensure online safety for our people.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Indeed, as more of our interactions and activities shift online, individuals and businesses will inevitably be exposed to digital risks, online harms and potentially unhealthy addictions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents today are concerned that easy access to Internet among our youths has made widespread dissemination of harmful and inappropriate content, such as pornography, quick and effortless.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But we all have a role to play, too.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond being digitally "book smart", we must also build "street smarts" to identify and avoid new risks in the online world.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are also looking to understand citizens' digital habits and gaps between attitudes and behaviours.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This will inform the development of more targeted interventions to improve digital adoption and address the needs of vulnerable segments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Finding solutions to help users protect themselves from harmful online content requires the expertise of diverse stakeholders, such as legal professionals, tech specialists, regulators, educators and community partners.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MCI is, therefore, working closely with our community partners to promote safe, responsible and positive use of technology.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In conjunction with Safer Internet Day on 8 February, the Media Literacy Council (MLC) partnered Apple Singapore to organise a cyber wellness webinar for Primary school teachers and launched a fun and relatable video-making challenge for students to encourage the sharing of cyber wellness messages.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond this webinar, MLC has also produced resources to help individuals avoid falling victim to technology-facilitated harms, such as scams, sexual grooming, pornography and online harassment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The council also promotes digital literacy resources to educate the public on being more discerning and empathetic online to create a safer, smarter and kinder Internet for all.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In September last year, TOUCH Cyber Wellness launched a programme entitled "e-Conversations for the Family", with a toolkit to guide parents in having conversations with their children about pornography and its dangers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The AfA aims to raise awareness of online sexual harassment and empower victims to address and deal with such incidents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Key insights will be released in due course.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The AfA has also partnered other stakeholders for greater outreach.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes a collaboration with DBS and the Singapore Judiciary on a community hackathon to generate solutions on creating safer and kinder online spaces, and the recently concluded Youth Action Challenge, where the AfA supported the mental well-being track.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We also marked Safer Internet Day with a webinar, where a panel of professionals discussed how parents and families can help our children and young stay safe online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Moving ahead, the AfA will continue engaging and equipping parents and youths to support those who may be experiencing online harm.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes a second online harms webinar which will take place in the coming months, as well as a website containing updates on the AfA's events and resources to address online dangers and risks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are especially grateful for the support of our 48 Alliance members, some of whom are keen to run initiatives to tackle online harms in the longer term.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MCI will continue to work with these partners to tackle online harms.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We welcome more stakeholders to join us in ensuring that all users are empowered to navigate the digital future with confidence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Just as we have built one of the world's safest, cleanest and most liveable cities, all of us have a role to play in shaping Singapore's online space.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We must preserve positive and enriching digital experiences for those around us by being respectful users online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In closing, I would like to put these various efforts in context.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This will allow all Singaporeans to partake in exciting opportunities with a spirit of discovery and growth in our shared digital future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Jessica Tan spoke about the opportunities in our Digital Economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Indeed, we saw the benefits of digitalisation, particularly over the last couple of years where firms and our workforce had to deal with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am heartened that many firms are embracing digital technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA's Digital Acceleration Index, an annual survey of more than 2,000 firms across 23 sectors, showed that digitalisation is picking up pace across our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Three in four firms now adopt at least one digital solution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And as we emerge from COVID-19, we will sustain this momentum in two ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, providing businesses, particularly our Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), with the tools and support to transform digitally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, by nurturing a future-ready workforce with the qualifications and skills to get into good jobs in the tech sector and progress well in their careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our firms want to adopt digital and transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is the consistent feedback when we engage industry associations and firms, as well as from various surveys that we conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, as Mr Christopher de Souza pointed out, SMEs face practical issues in raising their digital game.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: SMEs share with us their difficulty in building up their in-house IT team with the right experience and expertise; in helping them select solutions and vendors that meet their needs, while putting in place system and processes to protect their clients and operations from cyber threats and data breaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We must harness network effects to fully benefit from opportunities in the digital economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: SMEs, which comprise more than nine in 10 of our enterprises, account for almost half of our GDP and hires seven in 10 of our local workforce, are an important constituent in our national digital push.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, enabling secure and seamless digital transactions across the economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, supporting digital transformation of our industry sectors; and third, equipping firms with resources and tools to facilitate digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, on economy-wide digital enablers, or digital utilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Just like water or electricity in the analogue world, we can envisage a foundational set of systems or standards to facilitate seamless and secure transactions in the Digital Economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to put in place such digital utilities to support our businesses as they shift their operations and transactions online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, we will support the transformation of our industry sectors, building on these digital utilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We recognise that each sector faces unique challenges and operating contexts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have launched Industry Digital Plans (IDP) and these IDPs provide firms with a step-by-step guide on digital solutions and skills training curated for each stage of their growth, tailored to their sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will expand the coverage of the IDPs, and the next IDP to be launched will be for the legal industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to refresh these IDPs to incorporate new digital utilities, relevant technological advances and best practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we announced two schemes – CTO-as-a-Service and the Digital Leaders' Programme – to empower businesses on their digitalisation journeys.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This year, our enhancements will help SMEs raise their digital maturity, reach markets abroad and retain trust in the digital marketplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: On digital maturity, we will raise SMEs' digital maturity with advanced technological capabilities that are curated to meet their sectors' needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Launched in 2020, the Advanced Digital Solutions, or ADS scheme, helps SMEs access advanced technology and integrated digital solutions, such as robotics and aggregated data analysis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will grow our list of 30 solutions, with an emphasis on AI-enabled and cloud-based solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will also expand our Grow Digital scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through the Grow Digital programme, we have worked with Enterprise Singapore to curate a group of e-commerce platforms that can help our firms reach international markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This year, Grow Digital will bring more firms to global markets through a broader group of e-commerce platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Shawn Huang spoke about helping businesses protect themselves against cyberattacks and data breaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will launch the Cyber Trustmark and Cyber Essentials mark, and the Data Protection Essentials Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Obtaining the trustmarks would give businesses and their customers the confidence that certain cybersecurity and data protection standards have been met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage businesses to view these trustmarks as investments and a competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our Digital Economy efforts are powered by the Infocomm sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Seah Kian Peng spoke about helping our people seize opportunities in this digital economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Indeed, the growing and vibrant tech sector creates many good jobs and opens up many exciting opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Around 10,000 more ICT professionals have been added each year in recent years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our priority is to nurture a strong pipeline of local tech talent, including fresh graduates and mid-career workers, while ensuring our tech workforce remains relevant and competitive in this fast-changing digital space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the next three years, around 23,000 local students will graduate from our IHLs in Information and Digital Technologies, or IDT, courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In this regard, let me outline two important moves we are making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we will strengthen our pipeline of ICT graduates from our Universities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As a proportion of all degree places, the number of IDT places increased from 7% in 2010 to 18% in 2021, close to one in five.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will also establish new programmes and specialisations to support emerging tech needs in different sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: An example is the new Bachelor of Science in Applied Computing, with specialisation in fintech that will be launched this year by the Singapore Institute of Technology, in partnership with IMDA and MAS, and supported by financial institutions, including AIA and Standard Chartered Bank.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We look forward to working with other sector leads on different training modalities for specific skills needs for their sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, we will help our Polytechnic and ITE graduates enter tech roles through more structured pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Some Polytechnics and ITE IDT graduates shared with us that they cannot find suitable entry-level roles in their areas of study, while others encountered employers who preferred University graduates, even though our Polytechnic and ITE graduates are capable of doing these jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Structured support and clearly defined scaffolding in their career pathways can make a world of difference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I recently met Mr Muhammad Syurhan Bin Ja'afar, who graduated from our Work-Study Diploma programme in Data Centre Infrastructure & Operation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Syurhan graduated from ITE with a Nitec in ICT (Cloud Computing) and gained first-hand experience of the tech sector through his internship at NCS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, his family's financial situation meant that he had to forgo his plans to take up a diploma.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It was only later, with the encouragement of his Class Advisor, that he applied for the Work-Study programme and gained a place with the sponsorship of Racks Central Data Centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Syurhan shared with me that his company's support and a structured career pathway gave him the confidence to complete the course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will enhance the quality of internship opportunities for Polytechnic and ITE students, to apply their knowledge outside the classroom.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: After graduation, they will be able to take up apprenticeships at participating companies under place-and-train programmes, to learn the ropes of the ICT roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Participating companies will also establish skills-oriented training plans and pathways for tech roles for these graduates, including certifications and specialist training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These graduates interested in further studies will be supported through Work-Study Diploma or Degree programmes, spanning growth areas like AI, Cloud and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am heartened that companies like Accenture, GovTech, IBM, NCS and PSA Corporation have made significant commitments to provide internship, apprenticeship or placement opportunities and I urge more industry leaders to join this meaningful effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to fresh graduates, many enter the industry as mid-career workers, such as through the TeSA initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many joining the sector aim to progress in their careers, taking on higher value roles, such as product managers, software engineers or solution architects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We want to support these aspirations of our tech professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will partner industry leaders like Google, Microsoft and Grab, as well as large end-user companies like DBS, to groom product engineering talents for these roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Those on this specialist track will be trained in advanced technical skillsets like software and application development, data analytics, AI and Cloud, through both instructor-led and hands-on programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These tech professionals can look forward to taking on senior technical roles in their companies over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA will also launch the ICT Jobs Transformation Map (JTM) later this year, to help employers and employees across the ICT sector identify areas of high impact and the relevant reskilling or upskilling opportunities and training as needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I look forward to your continued support as we journey towards our shared digital future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: My colleagues have shared different facets of MCI's efforts to ready our ecosystems, businesses and people for a digital future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Minister Josephine Teo spoke about how MCI will enhance digital regulations for digital safety, security and resilience; and deepen engagement with Singaporeans to strengthen social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam shared about our continuing work to build a digitally-ready and inclusive society, such as through NLB's Libraries and Archives Blueprint 2025, which is showcased at the main lobby of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Minister of State Tan Kiat How spoke about our efforts to equip our workforce and enterprises with capabilities to seize opportunities in a digital and post-COVID-19 economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I will focus on three areas where we are investing for the future, to mark Singapore's place in the digital world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, building digital infrastructure to meet our future needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, pushing technological boundaries with leading edge innovation and research.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And third, fostering international partnerships to advance the digital economy and strengthen digital security beyond our shores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Shawn Huang and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about MCI's plans to ready our infrastructure for the next wave of digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The volume and complexity of digital traffic continue to grow very, very quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will increasingly rely on data and data-powered services, especially as cloud services and the Internet of Things (IoT) become more commonplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That means 463 billion gigabytes, which is equivalent roughly 60 hours of Netflix movies per person per day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How will we upgrade our digital infrastructure for a data age, so that it is fit-for-purpose and continues to support our needs?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To begin with, we must pay attention to our domestic telecommunications infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Wireless and wired network components, such as base stations and fibre optic cables, allow Internet traffic to flow seamlessly in large volumes, providing a high-speed service to every corner of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have continued to upgrade our local telecommunications capability, for example, through the shift to 5G. 5G technology enables unprecedented speeds and reduces the latency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, more data can be transferred at higher speeds. 5G networks are also more responsive and better able to cope with surges in data traffic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Here in Singapore, we continue to be at the forefront of 5G deployment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The characteristics and advantages of 5G allow for new use cases, such as in advanced manufacturing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) has been partnering IBM, Samsung and M1 in Singapore's first 5G Industry 4.0 trial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They will be deployed across IBM's global manufacturing sites from the second half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It relies on the human eye and it is subject to fatigue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It overlays images and text onto physical objects, allowing inspectors to identify defects in real time, augmented by this technological solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It also allows the operator to take photos and use deep learning algorithms that identify images to quickly detect factory defects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Apart from these wireless networks, we will also upgrade our wired networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Already, today, according to Internet metrics company Ookla, Singapore has one of the fastest broadband speeds in the world and we can look forward to more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The second category of infrastructure connects us to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These provide critical connectivity with international partners and allow us to be part of international data flows and digital trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore is already a digital connectivity hub and a preferred landing site for global submarine cable operators, due to our stable governance and advanced economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This connectivity enables the development of many different products and services and supports many businesses that choose to locate important operations here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It also allows our thriving research community to access computing resources from around the world and for our data centres and supercomputers to serve international partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to secure new landings to strengthen our international connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, Singapore-based maritime company, BW Group, plans to develop a new submarine cable pathway connecting Singapore to the US via Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The third category of infrastructure are data centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are vital nodes in the flow of digital traffic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Data centres power many applications and services for businesses and everyday life, from complex data management to e-commerce transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, the data centres are intensive users of water and electricity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Given our resource constraints, we need to manage the development of data centres sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore is committed to fulfilling our environmental obligations under the 2015 Paris Agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This comprehensive digital infrastructure, the various components that I have described, makes possible the provision of digital utilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are the services that ride atop the connectivity layers that have become essential and commonplace, allowing people and businesses to use digital services and transact seamlessly and safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Minister of State Tan Kiat How shared examples earlier, such as PayNow and InvoiceNow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other examples include the National Digital Identity, Singpass and TradeTrust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to invest in other essential digital tools and services and develop them as digital utilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Another digital utility is the Singapore Trade Data Exchange (SGTraDex).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, data is fragmented across the global supply chain ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With SGTraDex, supply chain ecosystem partners, such as shippers and logistics providers, are able to share trade data in a seamless and secure manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has been good with many companies across various sectors coming on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government and the Alliance for Action (AfA) for supply chain digitalisation are working with these companies on a Minimum Viable Product to allow more extensive data sharing and alive business environment, which will be launched later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our advanced infrastructure and highly used digital utilities can be vulnerable to attacks or risks of failure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree wholeheartedly with Ms Jessica Tan that we should ensure that our infrastructure is secure and resilient to address evolving threats and risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Minister Josephine Teo had earlier shared on MCI's efforts to secure important digital infrastructure and services through our Cybersecurity Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MCI also adopts design principles to embed security features and operational practices within the system architecture, rather than to add these at a later stage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One such technology is quantum communication, which promises to revolutionise the security of our information and infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Hackers leverage sophisticated techniques and powerful computing hardware to "crack the code".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As quantum computers mature, we can expect that adversaries will eventually be able to decrypt data and penetrate systems secured with today's technology simply by applying more and more computing power.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Quantum communication is secured by physics-based methods, such as quantum key distribution (QKD).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Potentially, this could help future-proof the security of our databases, critical systems and communications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This technique allows the creation of paired secret cryptographic keys, which are only held by the sender and the authorised receiver, anyone trying to intercept or copy the keys in between would introduce a detectable anomaly and this signals that the keys have been tampered with and then knowing that we can retransmit a new secure key in real time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If effective, this technique means that no amount of computational power would be able to break quantum-secured communications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It sounds a bit like science fiction, but quantum technologies have been developed in Singapore for over a decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since the Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT) was established at the National University of Singapore (NUS) in 2007, its researchers have contributed to 5,000 scientific papers, participated in projects supported by about $100 million in external grants and established several startups here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government continues to work closely with CQT to deploy quantum technologies in real-world applications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Two weeks ago, the National Quantum-Safe Network was announced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a public-private consortium that will deploy QKD-enabled wireless networks across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One of the spin-offs from CQT, SpeQtral, is commercialising a satellite that will allow for secure communication based on QKD technology, with support from EDB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When the satellite is launched and deployed into orbit, SpeQtral will be one of the first companies in the world to demonstrate a full commercial-scale solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I met the CEO, Lum Chune Yang, and his team last month and was very impressed by how they have followed through from their pioneering research and experiments, and together with the many commercial partners they have already lined up, such as Toshiba, to then bring this to life and come up with a commercially deployable solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Quantum technology is just one area of future communications which we are developing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This programme will accelerate the next bound of communications and connectivity research, such as in 6G.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The international research community recognises Singapore's strong innovation capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through this, parties will deepen research and development collaboration on 6G, such as through organising workshops, and conducting joint research and educational projects between the researchers of both institutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And just two months ago, we signed another MOU with the Korean Institute of Communications and Information Sciences in the Republic of Korea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other than investing in research, we are also strengthening the translation of research, so that companies and citizens can reap tangible benefits from these technologies today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Cybersecurity Industry Call for Innovation by the Cybersecurity Agency of Singapore (CSA) enables companies to solve cybersecurity problem statements with innovative solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The drive is powered by an AI co-processor and a special firmware that provides real-time data protection against software-based attacks, such as malware, ransomware and viruses, and physical attacks, such as unauthorised cloning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The X-PHY SSD continuously monitors itself without reading the stored files.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When the drive detects tampering, it locks itself and alerts the owner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This user-friendly solution does not require complex configuration or constant updating.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Lenovo has already teamed up with Flexxon to use these SSDs in some of its laptops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Alex Yam were interested in the new global opportunities as well as challenges and risks in the digital domain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Issues such as cybersecurity, data protection and AI ethics, are complex issues that transcend geographical borders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to build an international consensus on rules, norms and standards, so that the digital ecosystem is sustainable, interoperable and protected against both accidental and intended harms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members would be familiar with our Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) that exemplify this approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore has signed DEAs with four countries, most recently, with the UK last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also substantially concluded a DEA with the Republic of Korea in December 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng will be glad to know that Singapore's work with international stakeholders has been impactful and builds our global brand to be a trusted digital hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Internationally, we have made significant contributions to the cybersecurity community as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have been able to do so by drawing on our operational capabilities, technical expertise and innovation in cybersecurity and bringing these together with balanced policy and regulatory perspectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Critical to these efforts are the skilled and experienced cybersecurity personnel that represent us at many international discussions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Cybersecurity standards are one area where we are pushing ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has garnered interest amongst international partners, leading to an MOU with Finland for mutual recognition of cybersecurity labels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CSA and the Singapore Standards Council have also launched the first national standard, the Technical Reference (TR) 91, on Cybersecurity Labelling for consumer IoT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This can be adopted across the board by manufacturers, developers, testing bodies and suppliers of consumer IoT devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since December 2021, Singapore has assumed the chairmanship of the United Nations Open-Ended Working Group (OEWG) on Security of and in the Use of Information and Communications Technologies (ICTs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is the main international platform charged with international cybersecurity policy discussions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are facilitating discussions to achieve consensus on norms, rules and principles to advance a secure and interoperable cyberspace and encourage responsible state behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such efforts are all the more crucial, given the circumstances around the world.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We are ahead of time; so, you can have the time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are pushing to expand the recognition of these clauses in jurisdictions outside of ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In parallel, we are working to advance responsible AI deployment globally.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This will provide practical and implementable guidance to deploy AI responsibly and foster consumer confidence to use AI-enabled services in the region more widely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Harnessing opportunities in the digital space while managing the risks will be critical to our success and our survival.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Government and, through our partnerships, is putting in place various building blocks, with stakeholders, including digital capabilities, infrastructure, regulations, security and investments, for the future.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At the heart of our efforts lies our people, their potential and well-being.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have to aim for all Singaporeans to be empowered and to find fulfilment through their participation in the digital domain.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And, together, we will build a vibrant and secure digital future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: First, I would like to ask what are the types of harms to children that the new code of practice will be addressing.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Second, will views from parents and the community be sought so that the types of harms that children are exposed to can also be addressed in the new code?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: And third, an update on girls and women in technology, their progress and representation from schools, within the industry and even within the IMDA programmes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Can there be an update on how we have progressed and how we have fared so far?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms Tin Pei Ling for her three questions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will take the first two questions, not because the third one is unimportant – it is very close to my heart.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But today, for the purposes of the Committee of Supply debate, we would like to discuss the question of women in tech, together with how we are developing tech talent in general.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, Minister of State Tan Kiat How will address that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the question of what kinds of harm we are seeking to include in the codes, our aim is to ensure that our children can enjoy physical safety and emotional well-being.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, the question is, online – what harms them?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Parents all around the world will agree that they do not wish their children to be exposed to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think they could be and should be included in the codes that we are planning.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But there are also differences that depend on societal norms as well as family norms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, below what age are certain types of content considered to be inappropriate?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then there is, for example, the question of drug use.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some societies will find this more acceptable than others and we will have to cater for that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because of these differences, in particular, I see great value in us involving parents as well as the broader community in developing and designing the codes in the first instance and, in future, in updating the codes so that they stay relevant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MCI has some experience in dealing with this and we can take, broadly, the same approach that we take with other advisory councils that we have consulted on a regular basis for films, for publications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, we will continue to provide support to parents to help them protect their children online.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This would be through the programmes that the Media Literacy Council, as well as the NLB, put forward and these were described by Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam earlier.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms Tin Pei Ling for a very important question, about women and girls in the tech sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is well above the global average and we are very proud of it.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is supported by the community and, importantly, our industry partners.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Over the last few years, they have made very good progress in terms of raising the awareness that diversity and inclusion are better for business.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They have done many programmes to raise awareness and try and develop more girls and women in technology and established Singapore as a global leader in creating a supportive environment for women in tech.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It brought together over 600 women in the tech workforce for networking and mentoring events and, having received over 1,400 nominations for the Singapore 100 Women in Tech List in 2020 and 2021, they have identified the women leaders in our technology space who are role models and mentors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To a point that Ms Tin asked earlier in her cut, which I did not manage to reply to fully, I will just provide updates on Mentor Connect, which is a cross-company mentorship programme in which women professionals and leaders in those companies mentor students and other girls and women who are interested in a career in technology.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, they have done well and reached out to many more schools.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I encourage women tech leaders and companies to join us in this effort.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Chairman, I thank Minister Josephine Teo, Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, Minister of State Tan Kiat How and Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam for their replies.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: AI is an area with great transformative potential, fundamentally changing how our economy and society function, including jobs.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: What are the Government's plans to enable businesses and individuals to tap on the opportunities brought about by AI?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: And as AI deployment becomes more pervasive, how will the Government ensure responsible deployment of AI without stifling innovation?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Sharael Taha has asked a really important question on AI and, for a topic of this nature, we can actually have a full seminar on it and we would not run out of things to talk about.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But in the time that we have, perhaps let me just share with him some of the thinking that we have in the Government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These covered the areas of logistics, smart estates, education, healthcare and border control.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In November last year, the Deputy Prime Minister added two more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are the National AI programmes for Government and for the finance sector.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Here, I want to caveat, we are not just talking about efforts in the last three years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will be talking about efforts that preceded that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In terms of research capabilities, we are making headway.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if we look at the kind of research collaborations that tech companies have with our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) as well as the corporate labs that they have set up together, this attests to our research capabilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But in terms of the deployment into industries and businesses, I would say that it is quite uneven and also, I should add, there can be different types of AI being put to use.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the financial services sector, for example, machine learning is quite common today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You would find it particularly amongst the fintech companies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the transport sector, we are beginning to see more and more deployment of autonomous systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would say that within each sector, the beauty of it is that it is not always the case – in fact, it is often not the case – that the bigger companies are better at it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: New entrants are frequently more likely to experiment with new solutions provided by AI, because they are likely to be unencumbered by legacy systems and business processes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Sharael Taha had a second part of his question which is very important and that has got to do with the governance of it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is a big topic but I should say that IMDA not just has programmes to promote AI adoption, it also seeks to ensure that AI is used in Singapore with a degree of security as well as accountability.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And how are we seeking to do so?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In quick summary, quite early on, in fact, probably being one of the earliest countries to put out a Model AI Governance Framework, which has since been contextualised for different sectors in order to bring out the principles and practices and translate them into real actionable items in the sector.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are also developing an AI Governance Testing Framework and a corresponding testing tool kit to help AI systems owners and developers become more transparent about how their AI works.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I would say that we are making all of these efforts in the hope that, truly, our businesses and our people can benefit from the rich potential of AI.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think we have time for two or three more clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will call on Ms Jessica Tan first and then Mr Leong Mun Wai; and if there is any further clarification and we have time, then a third clarification.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: What I did suggest in my cut – and I did appeal – was for MCI and related agencies to look at communities of learning and communities of practice of tech talent coming together.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: You can say that they can come together today on their own.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: But I think that if MCI can play a key role in facilitating that and supporting those, it would allow for a lot of learning amongst a very rich base of tech talent and digital talent that already exists in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I hope that I can get some response to that.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms Jessica Tan for her suggestion and idea.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Behind the suggestion was really about having tech talent, basically tech professionals, coming together to share best practices, update one another on technological advances in this space, especially in this digital space which is evolving so quickly.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: New threats appear every day, cybersecurity data breaches as well as new practices in terms of how we apply technology, the kind of technical advances and innovation coming out from all over the world as well as Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And I think the spirit of that, is something that we will consider and look at.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: More importantly, I think it is working together with our industry associations, both the ICT companies and industry associations, SGTech, as well as the tech professionals' association, Singapore Computer Society, or SCS.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Today, we already work together with them to mount many training and upskilling courses for our tech professionals, bringing tech professionals together to discuss issues.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, is Web 3.0 reality or hype, whether NFTs are something that will be mainstream, what is the future for cryptocurrency, how we are thinking about cyber-attacks and cyber protection?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are topics and issues that we work very closely on with our industry partners, our industry association partners, SGTech and SCS, on many of these causes.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, certainly, we will take Ms Jessica Tan's suggestion and continue to expand on these areas.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Chairman, I have two clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But before that, I would like to clarify that I did not say SPH is a Government-owned company.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I hope the Minister will acknowledge that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: My first question is while SPH is not a Government-owned company, but the Government has considerable influence over SPH, the listed company, over the years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A quick check would confirm whether he said it was SPH or whether it was SPH Media Trust.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if I heard wrongly, I apologise to him.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But, in any case, his questions are quite strange because, if he insists that SPH Media Trust is Government-owned, why would funding even be an issue?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not something that we would have to come to Parliament and explain to Members about.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government does not own this company limited by guarantee and it did not own SPH, the listed entity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, the decisions of SPH, as a listed entity, must depend on its board and must, ultimately, depend on its shareholders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And a listed entity could not have invested the same kind of resources to keep it a viable, trusted institution that it is today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, we have basically two choices to make.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If I could seek Members' indulgence to articulate them again.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Accept that this media business existing within a listed entity could decline and we live with the consequences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Alternatively, we mount a serious effort, do everything we can to help it to transform so that SPH Media Trust can remain a trusted institution serving the public good.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we reject the former and we say it is the latter, then we have to just look at the kind of investments that are being made elsewhere in the world because we are not the only country in the world where the media business has been disrupted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And the funding that we are talking about, I recognise it is not a small amount, and that is why there has been full accountability to Parliament.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But it is just into the ballpark that we see elsewhere in the world.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are not figures that are out of whack when we look at other countries' investments, the kind of media businesses having to make the investments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it would appear to me that the fundamental difference is that Mr Leong, or the PSP, simply does not value our local mainstream media as much as the Government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I hope I am wrong but if Mr Leong or the PSP does not agree with supporting our local media, then I would really urge him to reconsider the position, whether it is wise for Singapore to do so.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Chairman, I have a clarification in relation to the library.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Currently, the National Library Board (NLB) has an app titled "Libby" which enables users to locate and borrow books and e-materials.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I just want to clarify or enquire whether the app can be further improved with more interactive and user-friendly features.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: For example, NLB can consider working with relevant agencies like Families for Life or NEA to create special thematic filters.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The categories of readers can be further segregated to wider groups to recommend books to suit different stages in life, for example, expecting mothers and children of different age groups.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The libraries are already working with various partners because this effort of curating and encouraging, piquing people's interest is something we need to tap on the community to provide that whole array and buffet of interesting content for library goers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, that is already something that is being done.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And as far as the technology is concerned, we have been working with different partners to develop and use the different platforms for different demographics.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are also working with people in the community to create learning communities within the library.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, the Member's suggestion is definitely something that can be taken in and something that we can consider.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I would like to just make a pitch, if you have not already, to go to the showcase and explore what are some of the other opportunities and we can work with partners on this.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think if you can make that clarification a quick one because I just saw Mr Pritam Singh's hand.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, if we have the time, I will give the time to Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: A quick clarification because I did not hear much about SME reskilling.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Just to make sure that they have opportunities too.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If Members recall, last year, in December, if I recall correctly, SkillsFuture Singapore came up with the Future of Skills for the digital economy.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And the number one skill that is in demand in the digital economy is really around technological application, that is, how to apply the skills to use the technology tool that an SME or a firm has put in place in its organisation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Having a tool is important, but to be able to use it effectively to achieve business outcomes is something that is really an important return on investment (ROI) that the SMEs need to think about.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In this regard, we have worked together with other agencies on a few areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Because the skill needs for different tools – applied in different sectors and different firms at different levels of digital maturity – will vary.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These skills plan and training roadmap will have to be customised for that archetype of firms.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And that will be as part of the industry digital plans.
